newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on KLM Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on KLM Q1 results.

text.p: Dutch airline company KLM on Tuesday reported first quarter 1997/98 net profit of 190 million guilders versus 271 million guilders and operating profit of 244 million guilders versus 80 million. Analysts had expected a first quarter net profit of between 94-136 million guilders. KLM also said it expected operating profits for the full 1997/98 year, ending March 30, to improve.
The following are a selection of analysts' comments:

"It beats my already positive expectations. The most important thing is that the operating profit has tripled. It looks like the Van Wijk effect is already there, although you have to bear in mind that the first quarter last year was very disappointing. The (forecast) statement is very positive, but it shouldn't be too hard to raise operating profits. The dollar and the pound are very helpful and they must benefit from oil prices that are lower than in the latter part of last year."

"The operating result looks good and was above expectations. The operational side of the business looks strong, but the strategic side is still a question mark as it is unclear what kind of alliance they might come up with. It was a surprise that the results of Air UK were fully consolidated already in the first quarter as the news they were buying the rest of Air UK is only a few weeks old. The effect of Air UK on the operating result was between 10 and 15 million guilders, what means that the overall operating result was still above expecations.

Cargo results were better than expected. The increase in the number of passengers was above expectations and financial charges dropped. Sentiment is positive and we will upgrade the earnings per share forcast. We upgrade KLM from underperformer to at least market performer."

"It's very positive. It was above our expectations and far above consensus. Almost everything seems to have worked in their favour -- the impact of currencies, fuel prices and greater transportation of passengers. They say they can do better and, with current economic conditions, they should be able to do. We currently have the stock as a hold, but we may have to reconsider that."
